A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SleepMaMi research. The complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material reorganized between appendices.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original sleep staging, breathing-event segmentation, disease prediction, few-shot, and ablation results.

after.justification: Original empirical results are retained and expanded with CFS/SOF evaluations, demographic subgroup analyses, and additional controlled comparisons in Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: The private/shared Micro-Encoder, bidirectional Mamba Macro-Encoder, hybrid reconstruction/contrastive objective, and DGCL procedure remain unchanged. Alternative architectures, pretraining objectives, and LSTM classifiers are evaluated as experimental alternatives rather than changes to the proposed foundation model.

E1.justification: V2 adds CFS and SOF as cohorts excluded from pretraining for sleep staging and SDB segmentation, including an older, entirely female SOF population. CFS also extends few-shot evaluation to both tasks. The original pretraining corpus and existing downstream coverage remain.

E2.justification: LaBraM joins the SHHS1/KISS comparisons in Tables 1–2. New comparisons evaluate SimCLR and DINO pretraining, SleePyCo, SleepTransformer and DistillSleep-T for staging, and AIX for SDB segmentation (Tables 16–19). SleePyCo appears only in the SHHS1 comparison; the original main-table comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds LSTM-classifier evaluation alongside linear probing, CFS few-shot sample budgets, and architecture controls using batch size 32 with peak-memory measurement. Section 3.3 also changes the stated normalization from all signals to all except SpO2. This establishes a reported preprocessing revision, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and demographic-factor ablations, v2 adds a configuration without MAE, cycle-length sensitivity, Macro-Encoder architecture/memory comparisons, and alternative pretraining objectives. Table 4 extends the Macro-Encoder analysis to disease prediction, while Appendix E adds disease-performance comparisons across demographic subgroups.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 continues reporting point estimates; demographic dispersion statistics follow the existing dataset-description practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 revise KISS staging accuracy/Macro-F1 from 62.8/60.6 to 71.0/70.0 and SDB accuracy/Macro-F1 from 81.8/75.4 to 85.5/78.0. Numerous external-cohort, LSTM, specialist, subgroup, and ablation results are added; the ISRUC accuracy curve is removed. Main SHHS1 and Table 3 results remain unchanged. The KISS revisions are not established same-setting gains: preprocessing wording changes, and unchanged Figure 11 still yields the earlier KISS scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and definitions in Equations 1–7 are substantively unchanged, and neither appendix adds proofs or theoretical results. Adding braces around the binary event indicator's values is a notation correction.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the performance claim from outperforming existing foundation models to outperforming or matching them; the contribution list also drops 'significantly.' The central claims about integrating micro- and macro-structure, DGCL, and label efficiency remain.

C2.justification: V1's KISS hardware-shift explanation and generalization caution are replaced by an interpretation of robust cross-hardware performance. V2 adds demographic-bias interpretations, acknowledges demographic-shortcut risks in the Impact Statement, and identifies the hand-designed DGCL distance as a limitation. Appendix E's assertion that DGCL does not amplify bias is stronger than its subgroup evidence supports.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code/checkpoint availability statement and repository pointer, CFS/SOF channel and sampling information, and implementation details for the new comparisons, including augmentation settings and DINO momentum. Most original architecture, hardware, and training specifications remain intact; Table 9 corrects '120 epochs' to '120 patches.'

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning beyond SleepFM and general time-series models to discuss SleepGPT, Sleep2Vec, OSF, LaBraM, and HiMAE. It more explicitly distinguishes SleepMaMi through its second-scale-to-full-night hierarchy. Additional references support the new cohorts, specialist comparisons, and DINO experiment.

P1.justification: Most method prose and the main section sequence are retained. Targeted passages are rewritten, Section 4.5 and acknowledgement/impact/conflict statements are added, and the former Appendix D material is reorganized across Appendices D–F. Author, affiliation, and publication-header text also changes.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the benchmark and dataset tables, adds columns or rows to existing analyses, and introduces Tables 11 and 14–19. Figure 5 changes from two ISRUC accuracy/F1 panels to three Macro-F1 panels covering ISRUC and CFS. Existing figures and appendix displays are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The external CFS/SOF evaluations and controlled architecture, cycle-length, and pretraining comparisons address important gaps in v1's evidence for generalization and design choices. LSTM and specialist comparisons also reveal comparative limits, substantially improving the paper's evidential support. Material weaknesses remain: revised KISS tables conflict with unchanged Figure 11, and Appendix E overstates fairness despite Table 11 showing a larger absolute sex gap for SleepMaMi than Micro-only (0.015 versus 0.003).
